about: Joint ranges and couplings for the anatomical hand (motion/hand_model.py) and arm (motion/arm_model.py). Degrees. Angles are anatomical: 0 = straight / neutral, + = flexion, abduction toward the thumb side (so the little finger's abduction is negative), radial deviation, pronation. Thumb CMC angles are measured from NIMBLE's relaxed MRI thumb, with the measured arcs placed around it. Every number's source and evidence level is in docs/hand-physics-plan-2026-10.md, section 3.

tenodesis.about: Two-joint finger muscles (plan 3.1): the long flexors and extensors cross the wrist, so in a relaxed hand bending the wrist back closes the fingers and bending it forward opens them. Each finger's relaxed MCP and PIP angle, linear in wrist flexion between wrist_deg's two ends; moonshot/body/skeleton.py makes each a spring along a fixed tendon across the wrist and the finger joint, so the finger's motor overrides it.
tenodesis.reason: At full wrist extension: Neumann 2009, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System, 2nd ed. (Mosby), ch. 8, pp. 266-267: complete wrist extension flexes a healthy relaxed hand's MCP joints about 35 deg, PIP 50 and DIP 20 (as cited by Sonune et al. 2024, Can Prosthet Orthot J 7(1):42879); DIP follows PIP by its own coupling. Proposed: the fingers straight at full wrist flexion, and linear between
tenodesis.stiffness_reason: Enough that a relaxed finger keeps its posture against its own weight (about 0.01 N m), and well under the fingers' servo stiffness (0.9-1.6 N m/rad, strength.json), so effort overrides it

body.about: Trunk and right-arm ranges for motion/body_model.py (conventions in its docstring). Provisional: literature active ranges, checked against the 1st-99th percentiles of GRAB+ARCTIC manipulation (motion/human_data.py).

comfort.about: Range-normalised comfort cost sum w*((q-centre)/half)^2 (Cruse 1990 U-shaped per-joint comfort; Santos/Marler normalisation). Centres/bands from Gates 2016 functional peaks, RULA bands (McAtamney 1993) and Morrey 1981; weight ordering from Kee & Karwowski 2001 (shoulder accrues discomfort fastest, elbow slowest). Pronation costs x3 beyond +/-45 of its centre (RULA 'near end of range'). Tuned 2026-10-28 after validation: trunk axial rotation x3 and humeral rotation x2 (centre 5) so the trunk stays within people's p99 (13 deg) and humeral internal rotation within Gates' <23 deg typical.

body.about_girdle: sc_prot / sc_elev are mm of glenohumeral-centre travel in the thorax frame (clavicle + scapula). Ranges: about +/-30 deg of sternoclavicular protraction/retraction and 0-35 deg elevation on a ~150 mm clavicle give roughly -25..45 mm forward and -15..35 mm up (textbook SC ranges; [unverified] exact values).
